text.text_excerpt: Love dabbling in this place whenever I am in NOLA. I'm always intrigued by the on-site praline making, although I was a bit disappointed not to see it happening this last weekend that I stopped in to pick up fresh pralines to take home to my mom. I am allergic to nuts so I honestly don't know if they are the best pralines ever, but Mom sure does love them and she is a tough critic when it comes to her sweets. BF always steals one from the box that I buy her so I guess that's confirmation that they're pretty good. We love to hangout and check out all of their trinkets and taste the hot sauces. Magnolia Praline Company was a fun find. We went twice. It's a great place for souvenirs, presents, and of course, the famous NOLA pralines. You can't go to NOLA without trying a praline. They are just about as NOLA as beignets are. Magnolia Praline Company makes their pralines on site and you get to sample them too! They have four different flavors from plain to spicy. I was not a fan of the spicy but the rum one was good. I wish I had bought some but I was on a budget. There are all sorts of things to buy at Magnolia Praline Company from soup mixes to aprons and hot sauces. We went home with a giant stuffed voo doo skeleton to gift to a teenager. It sounds strange but it was very cute. ...

This is a neat shop that has a lot of fun little treats. As the name suggests, they have pralines. I didn't try any, so I can't vouch for them, but I've discovered that if you've had one praline you've had them all. They also carry a variety of cooking supplies such as utensils as well as spices and hot sauces and things like that. The woman working was sure to ask if I needed any help or if I was looking for anything specific. This was nice, especially considering I had stopped in on a pretty busy night. Magnolia probably isn't worth going out of your way, but if you find yourself in the area, it's worth a look.
